newsitem.title: UK: Monthly review - Bombers strike Jerusalem, peace in jeopardy.
newsitem.headline: Monthly review - Bombers strike Jerusalem, peace in jeopardy.

text.p: On the last day of July, Israel suspended peace talks after two Moslem militant suicide bombers killed 13 people and wounded 170 in a Jerusalem market.
The NATO summit in Madrid invited Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic to join and the EU commission recommended those three plus Slovenia and Estonia for membership of the European Union.
Elsewhere, Italian fashion guru Gianni Versace was shot dead outside his mansion in Miami Beach. His suspected killer, Andrew Cunanan, committed suicide after a police hunt a few days later.
Hollywood mourned two of its biggest stars in two days with the deaths of Robert Mitchum and James Stewart.
Here is a chronology of the main events of the month:
July 1 - Thousands of democracy activists march through central Hong Kong in the first test of the right to protest since China took back the territory from Britain.
July 2 - President Leonid Kuchma of Ukraine accepts the resignation of Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko.
July 2 - United States begins a round of controversial underground nuclear weapons-related tests in Nevada.
July 3 - The 14-member Caribbean Community (Caricom) admits Haiti as the newest full member.
July 4 - Hardline nationalists ignore President Biljana Plavsic's order to disband the Bosnian Serb parliament and go ahead with a session which will try to remove her from power.
July 4 - The Pathfinder space probe makes a historic landing on Mars.
July 4 - A man who dies after undergoing plastic surgery in Mexico City is confirmed by U.S. sources to be Amado Carrillo Fuentes, the country's most wanted drug lord.

July 5 - Cambodian authorities impose a curfew in Phnom Penh after clashes in the city between forces loyal to the country's rival prime ministers. Late on July 6 Second Prime Minister Hun Sen ousts First PM Norodom Ranariddh and claims control of the capital on July 7.

July 6 - In Northern Ireland, hundreds of pro-British Orange Order members hold a controversial parade in an area inhabited by members of the rival Irish nationalist community. Nationalists riot in protest over the next few days.
July 6 - France's Gaullist RPR party elects former National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin as its new leader.

July 6 - In mid-term elections in Mexico, opposition parties break the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party's 68-year grip on the National Assembly and capture the key post of mayor of Mexico City.
July 7 - At least nine people are killed in Kenya when police break up demonstrations in various parts of the country.
July 7 - After days of heavy rains the first reports of flooding emerge from Poland. Over the rest of the month the floods spread across Poland, the Czech Republic and eastern Germany.

July 7 - Islamic fundamentalist leader Abdelkader Hachani is sentenced to a jail term in Algeria. He is released the next day as he has already been in detention since 1992 when the authorities cancelled elections his FIS party was poised to win.
July 8 - At least 33 are killed and 66 injured when a bomb explodes on a train in the Indian state of Punjab.
July 8 - North Korea declares an end to a three-year mourning period for "Great Leader" Kim Il-Sung.

July 8 - NATO summit in Madrid invites Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic to apply to join and gives a commitment to consider Romania, Slovenia and the Baltic states at a future date. On July 9 it launches the Euro-Atlantic Partnership Council.
July 9 - Ukraine signs a special charter with NATO that gives it the right to call for "consultations" if it faces any outside threat.
July 9 - Election results from the June 29 and July 6 Albanian elections show the ex-communist Socialists and their allies won at least 107 of 155 seats.
July 9 - Heavyweight boxer Mike Tyson is banned from the sport for a year and fined $3 million for biting opponent Evander Holyfield's ear during a June 28 world heavyweight title fight.
July 9 - Earthquake measuring 6.9 on Richter scale strikes the Caribbean coast of Venezuela, killing at least 79.
July 10 - British special forces shoot Bosnian Serb police chief Simo Drljaca dead trying to arrest him. They successfully arrest Milan Kovacevic, a hospital director, also on war crimes charges.
July 10 - Association of South East Asian Nations postpones Cambodia's membership due to the political situation there.
July 10 - European Commission cuts off aid to the Bosnian Serbs until their former leader Radovan Karadzic is arrested for war crimes.
July 10 - U.S. Senate approves George Tenet as Director of the CIA.
July 10 - U.N. Security Council agrees to retain sanctions against Libya over the 1988 Lockerbie bombing.
July 10 - Northern Ireland's pro-British Orange Order calls off some planned weekend marches, and re-routes others, to avoid confrontation with Irish nationalists.
July 11 - Thailand's worst-ever hotel fire kills 90 people at the Royal Jomtien Resort Hotel at Pattaya.
July 12 - Cuban government confirms identification that remains found in a remote Bolivian village are those of legendary guerrilla Ernesto "Che" Guevara. They arrive in Cuba on July 13.
July 12 - Rival factions battling in the Congo capital Brazzaville sign a U.N.-brokered ceasefire, coming into effect at midnight on July 14.
July 12 - Greek and Turkish Cypriot leaders end four days of "very positive" talks at the U.N. and are expected to meet again in August.
July 12 - U.S. President Bill Clinton leaves Denmark for home after a European tour which took in Poland, Romania and the NATO summit in Spain.
July 13 - Spanish politician Miguel Angel Blanco dies of his wounds after being found shot in the head the previous day. He had been kidnapped by the Basque separatist guerrilla group ETA on July 10.
July 14 - U.N. war crimes tribunal sentences Bosnian Serb Dusan Tadic to a 20-year prison term for his part in a vicious "ethnic cleansing" campaign against Moslem civilians in 1992.
July 15 - European Commission agrees that Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovenia and Estonia should join Cyprus in entry talks for the European Union's first expansion into eastern Europe.
July 15 - World-renowned Italian fashion designer Gianni Versace is shot and killed outside his mansion on Miami Beach.
July 17 - Hong Kong's China-appointed parliament passes bill suspending a clutch of labour rights laws pending a review and fresh legislation.
July 17 - Kocheril Raman Narayanan becomes first member of a low Hindu caste to be elected president of India.
July 19 - The Irish Republican Army guerrilla group announces a ceasefire, effective on July 20, in its 28-year war to end British rule over Northern Ireland.
July 19 - Military court in Jordan sentences army private Ahmed Daqamsa to life imprisonment with hard labour for killing seven Israeli schoolgirls in March.
July 19 - Bosnian Serb hardliners expel President Biljana Plavsic from their ruling party and demand she step down from office.

July 22 - Former SS officers Erich Priebke and Karl Hass are sentenced to 15 and 10 years imprisonment, although both terms were reduced because of mitigating circumstances. Hass goes free and Priebke faces 1-1/2 years in jail.
July 22 - Swiss banks list over 2,000 names of dormant pre-1945 accounts, including assets by Holocaust victims.
July 22 - President Boris Yeltsin rejects a controversial bill, opposed by the United States and Pope John Paul, that would have imposed tough new curbs on religious freedom in Russia.
July 23 - Slobodan Milosevic is sworn in as Yugoslav president, stepping down as Serbia's.

July 23 - Albania's president Sali Berisha resigns to join the opposition in the new parliament as it meets for the first time. On July 24 it lifts a curfew and state of emergency and elects Rexhep Mejdani as president
July 23 - Andrew Cunanan, suspected killer of Gianni Versace, is found dead on a Miami Beach houseboat.
July 24 - Charles Taylor is declared the new president of Liberia following elections on July 19.
July 24 - Irish President Mary Robinson announces she will step down on September 12 to take up a U.N. post.
July 24 - Sources in Algeria report that Armed Islamic Group (GIA) chief Antar Zouabri has been killed earlier in the week.
July 26 - Nine people die when a light plane crashes into a Red Cross tent at an air show in Ostend, Belgium.
July 28 - Leaders of Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities meet at the residence of the U.N. envoy Gustave Feissel - the first time the two leaders have met on home territory in nearly three years.
July 28 - Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu blocks the building of a Jewish settler enclave in the heart of Arab East Jerusalem, after it was given the go- ahead by local authorities.
July 28 - Film is shown of former Cambodian dictator Pol Pot going through a stage-managed trial in front of some 500 Khmer Rouge cadres in northern Cambodia.
July 28 - President Bill Clinton and Republican leaders reach an accord to balance the federal budget for the first time in a generation.
July 30 - In Israel two Arab suicide bombers kill 13 people in a crowded Jerusalem market. At least 170 people are injured. Israel suspends peace talks on July 31.
July 30 - United States lifts a 12-year-old ban on U.S. citizens visiting Lebanon after receiving pledges from the government in Beirut to do more to fight terrorism.

Notable deaths in July included: Sir Joshua Hassan, former chief minister of Gibraltar (1); Robert Mitchum, U.S. film actor (1); James Stewart U.S. film actor (2); Amado Carrillo Fuentes, Mexican drug lord (4); Italian fashion designer Gianni Versace (15); U.S. astronomer Eugene Shoemaker (18); Anglo-French entrepreneur Sir James Goldsmith (19); Antar Zouabri, Algerian Armed Islamic Group leader (22); Justice William Brennan, liberal U.S. Supreme Court Judge (24); Ben Hogan, U.S. golfer (25); Jaime Milans del Bosch, mastermind of aborted coup in Spain in 1981 (26); Seni Pramoj, three-times Thai prime minister (28).
